stories.headline: Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil, while Bolsonaro refuses to accept the result

sources.body:
Vanessa Buschschlüter Latin America and Caribbean editor

Flávio Bolsonaro had been expecting a victory tonight. His reaction to his election loss has been to question the result.

He said it was "impossible to recognise" even though with all of the results now in, he is trailing with 48.21% compared to Lula's 51.79%.

He is calling for an annulment of the election, and the reason he is giving is that "the rules of the game were changed".

What he is referring to is the decision by the Supreme Court to extend voting by two hours.

While it was an unusual decision, it was one which had been formally requested by both Lula and Bolsonaro's campaign teams.

Lula's team had argued that voters in São Paulo and Bahia could not get to the polling stations because of a lack of busses.

Bolsonaro's team cited heavy rain in some areas in the south of the country and in São Paulo as the reason for their request.

In his first public appearance, Bolsonaro said he would get his campaign's legal team to request the annulment.

No doubt the legal team is now busy hammering out the arguments it will put before the court to back up its claim.

sources.headline: Brazil's left-wing President Lula wins fourth term in surprise victory over Flávio Bolsonaro

sources.body:
Leftist incumbent Lula says unprecedented comeback was a ‘defeat for denialism’ as Bolsonaro refuses to accept election result

Lula wins election in stunning comeback – live updates

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , the Brazilian president, has staged a dramatic election fightback , defeating his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro , to claim a historic fourth term in power.

With 100% of votes counted the 80-year-old leftist received 4.4m votes more than Bolsonaro, with a 51.79% share to his 45-year-old rival’s 48.21%. However, soon after Brazil’s electoral authority confirmed Lula’s victory, Bolsonaro refused to concede defeat and asked for the results to be annulled.

Lula narrowly lost the first round of the election to Bolsonaro in early October, casting his political future into doubt and plunging progressive Brazilians into three weeks of despair. Never, since the return of democracy in the 1980s, has the first round runner-up won the second vote.

But Lula did precisely that on Sunday, prompting joyous scenes on the streets of São Paulo, where he had been following events, and at the hotel where he was watching the count.

Addressing a packed crowd of ecstatic supporters in a São Paulo conference hall, Lula said: “We are going to change the way that this country is governed … This election was a defeat for denialism … I want to thank God and to thank you, Brazilian men and women of this country … it was democracy that made this happen.”

After the result was confirmed, Alexandre Padilha, Lula’s health minister, said: “This is a huge victory for the Brazilian people who in the second round had the chance to think about what President Lula means for the environment, for the defense of our national health service and our education system and the Brazilian constitution. And the risks that the extreme right candidate entailed.”

“It’s a massive victory – not just for Brazil. It’s also an important signal to the rest of Latin America and to the world,” Padilha added.

The 8o-year-old appears to have made up much of the difference through what his allies had identified as his main opportunity: persuading his voters to turn out. After a record abstention rate of 21.08% in the first round, which disproportionately affected Lula voters because they tend to live further from polling stations, the rate fell to 19.21%.

Speaking during Lula’s victory speech, Bolsonaro said it was “impossible to concede the election result” and that his legal team would seek to have the election annulled.

Following in the footsteps of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro , who four years ago also refused to acknowledge his defeat to Lula – before attempting a coup and being convicted for it – the senator cited a supreme court justice’s decision to extend voting hours as the alleged reason.

His speech made no mention of the fact that his campaign had also asked the electoral court to extend voting hours, but he nevertheless said Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting by two hours to 7pm “was not normal, it was unacceptable” and amounted to “changing the rules of the game while the game was being played”.
sources.headline: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil president after historic upset over far-right Flávio Bolsonaro

sources.body: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, nearly 81 years old, clinched a fourth term in a tight runoff against Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday. The leftist leader won 51.7% of the vote, compared to 48.2% for the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, official results showed. Bolsonaro has refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote.
sources.headline: Brazil's Lula beats odds and seals re-election, rival Bolsonaro demands annulment

stories.headline: Serbia's Vučić concedes defeat to the student-led movement after historic turnout

sources.body:
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections.

"We still do not have final results... it is clear that we have lost these elections," the right-wing populist leader said as he conceded late on Sunday.

Preliminary figures from Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement. Celebrations erupted after Vučić conceded.

Vučić called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence.

Vučić had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017.

The Student List's lead candidate Ilija Srdanović told BBC Serbian: "This will be a free state."

He said the anti-corruption movement, which had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia, hoped to "free the country from tyranny".

There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle."

During a celebration speech, Student List candidate Radomir Saicic said Serbians had shown "no obstacle was greater than their will", Reuters reported. "No force can forever overpower a people who have decided to take their destiny into their own hands," he added.

Amid scenes of people dancing in the streets Belgrade, Selena Lebovic said the result was "really fabulous".

"We are all crying, and what to say. We couldn't believe that it would be so easy," she told Reuters.

Vučić made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade.

The centre of Novi Sad - the northern city that triggered the student-led protests - was crowded. "Everything is going to get better now," David Vasić, one of those celebrating, told the BBC Serbian.

The Student List - which has no obvious leaders and whose members are not used to politics - had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia.

It decided to field candidates to the 250-member parliament from across Serbian society including doctors, actors, academics and sports personalities.

The anti-corruption movement campaigned on a manifesto that included purging officials who broke rules cracking down on protesters, stopping party loyalists from leading public enterprises, and freeing the public broadcaster of political control.

Vučić and the SNS party have repeatedly denied corruption.

Vučić, who backs Serbia's candidacy for the European Union while refusing to impose sanctions on Russia over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, had pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare.

Preliminary figures provided by Serbia's election commission suggested a record high turnout, with 64.9% having cast their vote by 18:00 local time (17:00 GMT), two hours before polls were set to close.
sources.headline: Elation across Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić concedes to student-led protest movement

sources.body:
Vučić’s 12-year reign looks to have been ended by record turnout of voters in election provoked by student-led protests

The long-serving leader of Serbia , Aleksandar Vučić, has conceded defeat, ushering in a seismic political shift after a historic election that saw ​the increasingly authoritarian leader pitted against a student-led movement that had spent two years protesting against his government.

Vučić pointed to preliminary results that suggested voters had overwhelmingly backed the students, potentially giving them a majority in the country’s 250-seat parliament.

“We still do not have final ⁠results,” Vučić told supporters at his party headquarters in Belgrade. “On the basis of a sample … it is clear ⁠that we have lost these ​elections, the Student ‌List has ‌won, they will have between 135 ‌and 140 seats and we will have 105.”

A representative sample by the ​CeSID-IPSPS pollsters suggested that the ​Student List’s candidate list will have ​138 deputies, while Vučić’s rightwing Serbian Progressive party (SNS) garnered 104 seats. The remaining seats ‌were likely to be shared ​between ethnic ​national minority parties, said the pollsters.

As news broke that Vučić’s 12 years in power had come to an end, celebrations erupted on the streets of Belgrade and other cities.

In the capital, Ivana, 43, was ecstatic. “This feels like New Year’s Eve to me, like three New Year’s Eves all at once, really,” she said. “We can finally breathe again.” She added that she was hoping for swift accountability for top members of the ousted regime, a key campaign pledge from the Student List.

Others offered handshakes, high fives and hugs to police officers in the streets, while a chorus of honking horns rang out from passing cars.

At the headquarters of the Student List, supporters chanted “Victory, victory!” as they applauded, cried and traded hugs. “Dear Serbia, tonight the voice of the people is being heard,” said Radomir Saičić, a professor at Belgrade University, speaking on behalf of the students at their headquarters. “Tonight we celebrate victory, tomorrow we build the future.”

The scenes of joy came hours after a record number of voters turned up to cast their ballot on Sunday. Across the country, long lines snaked out of polling stations, with some reporting wait times of up to two hours. By 7pm local time pollsters and monitors CeSID and Ipsos put the turnout at 67.6%, the highest since the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1992.

The high turnout, along with the estimated 150,000 people who flocked to the students’ final pre-election rally last week in Belgrade, fuelled early speculation that the students may have rallied enough support to launch a new political era in the Balkan country.

In the lead-up to the vote, opinion polls had varied wildly, with analysts pointing to the high degree of uncertainty at play as the candidates representing the grassroots student movement went up against Vučić’s SNS.

The results were watched across the world as part of 10 pivotal days of elections across the globe in which the authoritarian right is facing off against pro-democracy forces. The victory for the student-led movement in Serbia is also likely to reverberate across Europe, adding momentum to the youth and student protests that have rocked cities across the continent.
sources.headline: Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić ousted by student movement in seismic election

sources.body: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in an historic election on Sunday following a near to 70% turnout at polling stations – the highest since the break-up of Yugoslavia in 1992. The snap election followed nearly two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the ‌city of Novi Sad in 2024.
sources.headline: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat in historic snap election with record turnout

stories.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returns from exile

sources.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile.

"I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail.

In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro.

The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US.

Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands.

She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters have lined the route of her journey to the capital.

She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of the sunroof of a car as she entered Caracas late on Sunday night.

Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: "I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil."

"Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" González said.

He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country "toward freedom".

An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied.

It's unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she's back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held . Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted.

A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election - held outside the Maduro government's official election authority - in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote.

Despite winning the primary, Maduro's government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize.

In the 2024 election, Machado's ally González ran in her place against Maduro.

The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public.

The opposition argued that González won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence.

Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty.
sources.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile

sources.body:
Nobel peace prize winner’s return after almost a year in exile is unlikely to please interim president Delcy Rodríguez

The Venezuelan opposition leader, María Corina Machado , has announced she has returned to Venezuela almost a year after she left the country to receive the Nobel peace prize.

“I’m here. With you,” she wrote on X on Sunday lunchtime.

Her close ally Edmundo González, who is in exile, confirmed her arrival. “Venezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil,” he posted on social media.

“Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” he said, adding that he too would soon return.

It was not immediately clear how Machado, 59, had managed to return to Venezuela but footage on social media showed she was in Barquisimeto, the capital of Lara state, which is about 220 miles west of the capital, Caracas.

Images showed her surrounded by supporters holding mobile phones in the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess church.

Footage posted on social media by her close ally Pedro Urruchurtu showed hundreds of supporters gathered outside the church to greet her, shouting: “Freedom! Freedom! Freedom!”

The Trump administration had reportedly opposed Machado’s return, believing her presence would complicate the cosy relationship it has struck up with the interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, since abducting her former boss, Nicolás Maduro, in January.

Machado and Rodríguez are political arch-rivals.

Machado slipped out of Venezuela last December – a few weeks before Maduro’s capture – and in recent months has reportedly made more than half a dozen failed attempts to return home, including after the devastating earthquake that hit the northern coast in June.

After Maduro was seized, many had expected Donald Trump to give Machado his blessing to take power. Her movement is widely believed to have beaten Maduro in the 2024 presidential election, but he refused to hand over power.

Instead the US president embraced Rodríguez, Maduro’s vice-president, who now governs a country widely seen as a US protectorate.

Machado has repeatedly heaped praise on Trump for launching the operation to remove Maduro, and gave him her 2025 Nobel peace prize medal, which she had been awarded for her peaceful challenge to Venezuela’s authoritarian government.

Asked by reporters on Sunday about her return, Trump said: “I don’t know anything about it, but I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel prize, so how can I say anything else?

“I hope she’s safe. She’s a very nice woman. But we’re doing very well in Venezuela.”

The US secretary of state​, Marco Rubio, claimed credit for creating the conditions that allowed Machado’s safe return after 10 months in exile.

Her return “is the direct result of the U​S​-supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile”, he said.
sources.headline: Exiled opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to Venezuela

sources.body: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado announced on Sunday that she has returned to her homeland following almost a year in exile, after covertly leaving Venezuela in late 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. She returns as doubts about her country’s democratic future and the role of the US are growing.
sources.headline: Opposition leader Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months in exile

stories.headline: China's leadership prepares for a key party meeting amid scrutiny of Xi Jinping's corruption campaign

sources.body:
The fifth plenum comes against a backdrop of years of purges that have had some analysts wondering if the issue is corruption or a lack of loyalty

When Xi Jinping came to power in 2012, he pledged to stamp out corruption all through the ranks of the Communist party. More than a decade later, the pace of investigations has not slowed. Last year, China’s disciplinary authorities opened investigations into more than 1 million people, including more than 100 officials at or above ministerial or provincial level.

As Chinese Communist party (CCP) officials kick off an important meeting this week, discipline – and party loyalty – is high on the agenda. For those who try to read the tea leaves of elite Chinese politics, concern about the apparent lack of discipline is dominating CCP discussions.

The “fifth plenum” began on Monday and is set to focus on “major issues on advancing the party’s full and rigorous self-governance”, according to a Chinese state media. In party-speak, “governance” is a byword for discipline, loyalty and anti-corruption .

As Xi continues to crack down on corruption, the fact that investigations nearly always result in a conviction begs the question over whether targets are truly guilty of corruption, or are they just political rivals to the people in charge.

Kerry Brown, director of the Lau China Institute at King’s College London, explained that in Xi’s worldview, which is obsessed with discipline and loyalty, there may not be much difference between the two. “If you’re corrupt, you’re not politically loyal. If you’re politically loyal, you’re not corrupt,” Brown said.

He added that in the CCP system, “corruption is not just material things”, but also “spiritual corruption”, which includes political disloyalty.

Some analysts argue that the reason that the anti-graft drive is so enduring is because corruption is a feature rather than a bug of an authoritarian, top-down political system with a sprawling bureaucracy that governs 1.4 billion people.

Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at the Asia Society thinktank, said: “Xi has made the party less corrupt and strengthened his control, but he knows that tougher punishment cannot fully resolve the problem of officials putting their own interests ahead of the party’s.

“Xi’s answer is to keep tightening discipline, making anti-corruption a permanent method of governing with no obvious point at which he can declare the job done,” Thomas said.

The job may be never ending, but the plenum is an opportunity to refocus the party’s energy on discipline. The fifth plenum is the fifth of seven gatherings that normally happen in every five-year cycle between CCP congresses. The plenums bring together more than 300 members of the CCP’s Central Committee, the most senior officials in the party hierarchy.

The meeting is particularly significant because it is likely to be the last substantive meeting before next year’s 21st Party Congress, where a new Central Committee will be chosen, and where Xi is expected to be anointed for a fourth term as the head of the CCP.
sources.headline: Xi Jinping’s corruption crackdown in the spotlight as China prepares for meeting of top leaders

stories.headline: Israel closes West Bank crossings as the country prepares for a pivotal election

sources.body:
All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements.

The restrictions come amid a crackdown in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the territory.

The Israel Defense Forces announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday.

It said most workers would also be barred from settlements from Sunday, with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas.

Before the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel. Since then only a small fraction have had their permits restored.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major operation on Friday in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed.

The Israeli military have been demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron, with hundreds of families having been displaced .

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation, which has led to at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened, according to footage shared online.

Even before the entry and exit bans on workers were announced by the IDF on Sunday, the military had cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents.

It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis in the West Bank - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.

Friday's shooting came during a tense time for the region, just days ahead of Israel's election taking place on Tuesday.

In an interview with Israel's i24 television channel released on Saturday, Netanyahu threatened a "very big surprise" for the Palestinian Authority (PA), which governs parts of the territory.

Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said the operation was being "driven by the elections" and that Netanyahu and his ministers were attempting to secure the votes of the far right and the settlers.

On Saturday, thousands gathered in Tel Aviv for a large anti-government demonstration.

The protest was organised by the October Council, a group founded by the families of victims and hostages taken by militants on 7 October 2023, to demand accountability for the failure to prevent the Hamas-led attack.

"Three days before the election, we will hold the culminating event marking three years of struggle to uncover the truth, demand accountability, and establish a state commission of inquiry," the October Council wrote on X ahead of the rally.

The gathering saw the participation of the leaders of the four main opposition parties, including Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief of staff who is neck and neck with Netanyahu.
sources.headline: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates

stories.headline: Appeals court questions the Trump administration's challenge to California voter rolls

sources.body:
Judge questions the Trump administration’s efforts to exert greater influence over elections process ahead of upcoming midterm vote.

A United States appeals court has expressed doubt over the Department of Justice’s lawsuit against California, which seeks to force the state to throw out mail-in ballots it has deemed likely to go to non-citizens.

Circuit Judge Mark Bennett said on Sunday that the three-judge panel would issue a decision as soon as possible, following a rare weekend oral argument.

But Bennett, an appointee of Republican President Donald Trump, voiced concern that the lawsuit would not hold up to scrutiny.

He pointed to the Elections Clause in the US Constitution, which allows states — not the federal government — to administer elections.

“It seems to me that you want us to issue an injunction that is entirely inconsistent with the law that the California legislature has adopted pursuant to the Elections Clause,” Bennett told Justice Department lawyer Matthew Donnelly. “How can we do that?”

The case is part of a larger effort under the right-wing Trump administration to crack down on alleged non-citizen voting ahead of the crucial November 3 midterm elections.

On October 15, less than three weeks before the midterm races, the Justice Department issued a complaint targeting California, a left-wing stronghold.

It asked the federal court system to set aside thousands of mail-in ballots that the government says were sent to “likely non-citizens”.

The lawsuit indicates the Trump administration sent California officials a list of 20,000 names it believes are not eligible to vote, based on citizenship.

Trump has often pushed the discredited claim that the Democratic Party is benefiting from widespread voting by non-citizens.

California has long been one of the targets for his election misinformation.

Earlier this year, Trump denounced the state’s primaries after right-wing candidates like Los Angeles mayoral hopeful Spencer Pratt felt short of his expectations.

“There’s BIG cheating by the Dumocrats in California,” he wrote on social media at the time.

He then announced that the state would be under investigation from the US attorney’s office.

Trump’s efforts have caused alarm, with critics accusing him of seeking to dampen voter turnout through intimidation and confusion.

The midterms will decide which party controls the US Congress, as well as key state and local positions.

Polls, however, predict steep odds for Republican candidates, given Trump’s souring approval ratings and dissatisfaction with issues like the cost of living and the US-Israeli war against Iran.

Voting rights advocates have warned that the Trump administration has not publicly revealed how it has compiled its list of non-citizen voters, and whistleblower reports have cast doubt on the accuracy of such lists.

In response to the October 15 lawsuit, California has countered that it has strong safeguards to prevent non-citizens from voting.

It also said that the Justice Department’s claims are based on dubious data.
sources.headline: US appeals court sceptical of Trump’s lawsuit over California voter rolls

stories.headline: Data-center backlash emerges as a growing political risk before the midterms

sources.body:
Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.

These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.

They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.

But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.

In the US, they've become a huge issue ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, with both Republicans and opposition Democrats coming out against their development.

It's putting opponents of data centre expansion on a collision course with US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed the pushback as a "sick conspiracy", even as public anger grows.

Here's what you need to know about the data centre boom, and why opposition is growing.

There are about 12,250 data centres around the world, according to Data Center Map , a company that tracks both operational and pre-operational sites.

That's up sharply from 2021, when there were around 8,000 operational sites.

As the chart below shows, data centres are most densely clustered in the US which has 4,767 sites. It is followed by Europe, where the UK and Germany lead.

Data centres have typically been located near to cities where it's easier to access high voltage power lines or water resources for cooling. But as they get bigger, more are being built in rural areas.

But when it comes to actual capacity, the US is ahead by a much larger margin, with China in second place and Europe lagging far behind.

This gap is set to widen in the coming years, leading some to warn Europe risks missing out on the potential economic benefits of the AI boom .

Data centres vary wildly in size, ranging from ones that fit inside a garden shed to others covering vast expanses of land.

The world's largest operational data centre is widely reported to be one run by China Telecom in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, covering an area of approximately one million square metres (10.7 million sq ft). That is equivalent to about 140 Fifa football pitches.

However, much larger sites are under construction as the graphic below shows.

All these sites are being built exclusively to provide the immense computing power needed to run AI services.

For instance, Colossus 2, which is part of the wider Colossus campus, will house hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips made by tech giant Nvidia.

It will also be used to train xAI's chatbot Grok. Elon Musk's company will use 41 methane gas turbines to help power the site, which activists say could "significantly increase" local air pollution . Local regulators say the turbines will meet air quality standards.

The pressure data centres put on local resources has sparked increasing concern. These facilities can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, which could lead to water shortages , some experts say.
sources.headline: Data centre debate heats up ahead of US midterms - here's what you need to know

stories.headline: Trump administration moves to expand psychedelic treatment for veterans with mental illness

sources.body:
No regulator has found the drugs safe or effective, but a VA official says as many as 2.1 million ex-service members could find them helpful.

President Donald Trump's Department of Veterans Affairs is looking to expand access to psychedelic medicine for 2.1 million veterans struggling with mental health conditions like post-traumatic stress disorder. | Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images

Nearly one in three veterans who relies on the government for health care could benefit from taking psychedelic drugs like magic mushrooms or MDMA.

That’s not the assessment of some hippie or fading 1960s rock star. It came from Andrew Gradison , a senior adviser at President Donald Trump’s Veterans Health Administration. Gradison told a conference for psychedelics enthusiasts this month that he is eager to ramp up the VA’s capacity to give the drugs to as many as 2.1 million veterans with mental illnesses like post-traumatic stress disorder or depression. Gradison said 6.4 million veterans regularly rely on the VA for care.

No government regulator has deemed psychedelics safe or effective for mental illness. Under former President Joe Biden , the Food and Drug Administration in 2024 resoundingly rejected a proposal to authorize MDMA — also known as ecstasy — combined with talk therapy, to treat people with PTSD.

But psychedelics are getting a second chance in the Trump administration. Trump in April issued an executive order to accelerate research, clinical trials and patient access to the drugs. Republicans in Congress are among psychedelics’ biggest backers. And the constituency they are seeking to please, veterans, are disproportionately Republicans.

Delivered daily by 10 a.m., Pulse examines the latest news in health care politics and policy.

sources.headline: The Trump administration moves to treat millions of mentally ill veterans with psychedelics

stories.headline: At least 83 injured, including seven seriously, after a bus plunges down an embankment near Barcelona

sources.body:
Al menos 83 personas han resultado heridas, siete de ellas graves, al despeñarse el autobús de línea en el que viajaban por un terraplén de 20 metros en la carretera BV-5114 a su paso por Fogars de Monclús (Barcelona).

El accidente ha ocurrido hacia las 16:43 horas de este domingo cuando, por causas que se están investigando, el autobús ha acabado saliéndose de la carretera, una vía estrecha de curvas, y precipitándose por un talud.

Según las cifras que ha dado a conocer la consejera de Salud, Olga Pané, hay 58 personas en situación leve; 18, menos graves, y 7 graves . Los heridos han sido trasladados a hospitales de Granollers (Barcelona), Josep Trueta de Girona y Vall d'Hebron de Barcelona.

Por el momento, no hay ninguna víctima mortal, pero tanto la consejera como el inspector jefe de intervención de los Bomberos, Santi Lleonart, han señalado que no puede descartarse que haya alguna, porque por la orografía de la zona podría haber alguna persona que haya sido despedida lejos del vehículo o incluso arrollada. A lo largo de la noche se trabajará en la zona, de difícil acceso y "muy inestable", según Lleonart, para determinar si puede haber más afectados.

El accidente, que ha obligado a activar en fase de alerta el plan de emergencias por accidentes en transportes Procicat, ha movilizado a 23 ambulancias, dos helicópteros medicalizados y tres equipos conjuntos de servicios sanitarios y Bomberos, que también han desplazado una treinta dotaciones y especialistas en rescates de montaña del grupo GRAE.

En cuanto al número de viajeros del autobús, con 65 plazas para personas sentadas , Santi Lleonart ha reconocido que no se sabe el número exacto, porque se trata de un vehículo lanzadera, entre un cámping y Fogars de Monclús e iba haciendo paradas intermedias y recogiendo gente.

Algunos de los pasajeros que viajaban en el autobús han salido por su propio pie del vehículo y han subido el terraplén hasta la carretera, mientras que otros han quedado atrapados y han tenido que ser evacuados por los equipos de emergencias.

El autobús siniestrado, de la compañía de transportes de viajeros Sagalés , cubría la línea 573, entre la estación de Rodalies de Sant Celoni y el centro del parque natural del Montseny en Santa Fe.

En un comunicado, la compañía ha dicho que está colaborando con los servicios de emergencia y las autoridades competentes y se ha puesto a su disposición para facilitar "toda la información necesaria para esclarecer las circunstancias del accidente".

Los Mossos d'Esquadra han cortado la carretera en ambos sentidos de la circulación, para facilitar las tareas de gestión del accidente. Posteriormente, procederán a investigar las causas de este siniestro, en el que no se han visto afectados más vehículos.

Protección Civil, en colaboración con Cruz Roja, ha habilitado un centro de acogida en Sant Celoni (Barcelona) para acoger a los viajeros del autobús accidentado pero que no han quedado heridos en el siniestro.

El presidente de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa , ha trasladado su apoyo a los afectados por el accidente. "Estoy en contacto permanente con las conselleres Núria Parlon y Olga Pané para conocer la evolución de la situación", ha escrito en una publicación en 'X'.
sources.headline: Al menos 83 heridos, siete de ellos graves, al caer un autob�s por un terrapl�n en Fogars de Montcl�s, Barcelona

sources.body:
Bomberos y equipos de emergencia durante las tareas de evacuación de los pasajeros

Un autobús atestado de pasajeros que volvían de pasar el día en el parque natural del Montseny se ha salido de la carretera y ha caído por un escarpado barranco por causas que aún se desconocen este domingo, cuando faltaban 17 minutos para las cinco de la tarde.

Un total de 83 personas habían sido rescatadas hasta el momento, aunque los servicios de emergencia no descartan que algún viajero haya podido salir disparado fuera del vehículo o incluso que se encuentre alguna víctima mortal debajo del autobús accidentado. Siete de los heridos estaban graves y han sido trasladados a hospitales, otros 18 tienen consideración de heridos menos grave y los 58 restantes, leves.

La mayoría de estos últimos han salido del autobús por su propio pie y han subid por el talud hasta la vía en la que se produjo el accidente, la BV-5114, la principal carretera que atraviesa el Montseny. Los que tenían peor pronóstico, en cambio, han tenido que ser evacuados en los dos helicópteros medicalizados del Sistema d’Emergències Mèdiques (SEM) que se han sumado a los dos helicópteros del grupo de actuaciones especiales de montaña de los bomberos para dar apoyo a la treintena de dotaciones terrestres que se han desplazado hasta el lugar del accidente.

El autobús ha caído 20 metros por un talud del término municipal de Fogars de Montclús lleno de árboles y rocas, “un lugar de difícil acceso y que mantiene el autobús en una situación muy inestable”, según el responsable del operativo de los Bombers, Santi Lleonart. De hecho, uno de los primeros objetivos ha sido apuntalar el autobús para hacer la evacuación con seguridad.

Aun así, la consellera de Salut, Olga Pané, ha comparecido cuatro horas después del accidente y ha asegurado que “por lo escarpado del terreno, cuesta saber si hay algún pasajero fuera del autocar”. Los drones y los perros de rastreo peinan la zona de 30 metros alrededor del autobús, aunque no será hasta esta mañana, con luz natural, cuando se dará por definitivo que no hay más heridos o incluso fallecidos.

El autobús accidentado era de la línea 573 del Bus Parc del Montseny, un servicio operado por la compañía Sagalés y que actúa como lanzadera entre la estación de tren de Sant Celoni y Santa Fe del Montseny, haciendo parada en el centro de interpretación del parque. Forma parte de una concesión de la Generalitat que funciona los fines de semana y días festivos, con la que se trata de incentivar el uso del transporte público en detrimento del vehículo privado para acceder a uno de los paisajes más populares en otoño, cuando se ve desbordado por la gran cantidad de coches que quieren acceder.

El tipo de vehículo tenía capacidad para 65 pasajeros sentados, pero el recuento preliminar eleva la cifra a 83 heridos. Como es habitual en los días con más demanda en este servicio, había gente que iba de pie en el pasillo al subir y encontrarse todos los asientos ocupados. Es una cuestión que la Generalitat permite en trayectos de menos de 50 kilómetros pese a que muchos pasajeros se sienten inseguros al hacer viajes en esas condiciones por la autopista a gran velocidad o en trazados con muchas curvas como el del accidente.
sources.headline: Al menos 80 heridos, 7 graves, al caer un autobús desde veinte metros en el Montseny

sources.body:
El accidente entre un autobús y un coche en Fogars de Montclùs (Vallès Oriental), ha dejado al menos 80 heridos, siete de los cuales graves, este domingo. En concreto, 58 personas han resultado heridas leves y otras 18 se encuentran en estado "menos grave". Tras el impacto, el autocar de línea de la empresa Sagalès se ha precipitado por un terraplen de unos 20 metros . Por el momento, no constan víctimas mortales entre los pasajeros. Los Mossos d'Esquadra investigan las causas del accidente , que se ha producido en pleno parque natural del Montseny.

En el lugar del siniestro se ha deplegado un amplio dispositivo de los equipos de emergencia. El Sistema d'Emergències Mèdiques (SEM) de Catalunya ha activado 23 ambulancias , dos helicópteros medicalizados y tres equipos conjuntos con los Bombers de la Generalitat. Los bomberos, por su lado, han desplazado hasta ese punto del Vallès Oriental 30 dotaciones , entre las cuales otro dos helicópteros para ayudar en las tareas de rescate y de traslado de los heridos. También se han acercado hasta el lugar de los hechos para asistir a los heridos, regular el tráfico e investigar las causas del accidente. El primer aviso del incidente se ha producido a las 16.43 horas , y el 112 ha informado que finalmente ha atendido a 25 llamadas relacionadas con este accidente.

La mayoría de los pasajeros, alrededor de un centenar y muchos de ellos de pie, ya ha podido abandonar la zona del accidente. De hecho, según han informado los Bombers, algunos pasajeroa ya habían podido salir por su propio pie del autocar. Sin embargo, la profundidad del barranco por el que se ha despañado el autobús ha hecho complicado las tareas de rescate de los heridos y de aquellos viajeros que habían quedado atrapados. Los bomberos han desplazado desde el terraplén hasta la carretera tanto por tierra como con la ayuda de sus helicópteros.

Cuatro de las personas heridas han tenido que se trasladadas a algún hospital. Los heridos se han repartido entre el Hospital de Granollers, el Hospital Trueta de Girona y la Vall d'Hebron.

Protecció Civil, que ha activado la alerta PROCICAT por el accidente, ha hbailitado un centro de acogida en Can Ramis, en Sant Celoni, para atender a las personas afectadas. También se han puesto a disposición de los pasajeros el servicio de profesionales de apoyo psicológico y se han movilizado voluntarios de Protecció Civil de municipios cercanos al incidente como Santa Maria de Palautordera, Sant Pere de Vilamajor, Montmeló o Lliçà de Vall, que han ayudado a garantizar el acceso hasta el Centro de Comando Avanzado (CCA) que han desplegado los bomberos en el lugar del siniestro.

La carretera BV-5114, donde se ha producido el accidente, está cortada "totalmente" entre Fogars de Montclús y Arbúcies, según ha informado el Servei Català de Trànsit (SCT).

El autobús implicado el accidente era de la línea regular 573 de Sagalés, que va desde Sant Celoni hasta Santa Fe del Montesny. Se trata de una ruta que discurre casi en su totalidad en el parque natural del Montseny y, de hecho, el siniestro se ha producido tras pasar por la parada del centro de información de Fogars de Montclús, uno de los principales accesos a los caminos rurales de la reserva natural.

stories.headline: Madrid's central-government delegate resigns after being left off the PSOE election lists

sources.body: <p>Francisco Martín Aguirre ha presentado su dimisión como delegado del Gobierno en la Comunidad de Madrid, cargo que ejercía desde marzo de 2023, han avanzado fuentes socialistas a EL PAÍS. El dirigente del PSOE ha justificado su renuncia con el argumento de que “no se dan las condiciones para seguir ejerciendo su responsabilidad”, según fuentes de la Delegación. El paso atrás de Martín se produce después de que se quedara fuera de las listas al Congreso y el Senado para las elecciones generales del 29-N. Martín apoyó de forma tácita <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-07-19/reyes-maroto-se-impone-como-candidata-del-psoe-a-la-alcaldia-de-madrid-frente-a-enma-lopez.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-07-19/reyes-maroto-se-impone-como-candidata-del-psoe-a-la-alcaldia-de-madrid-frente-a-enma-lopez.html">la candidatura de Enma López en las primarias en las que Reyes Maroto fue elegida el pasado julio candidata a la alcaldía de Madrid.</a> </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-10-25/el-delegado-del-gobierno-en-madrid-dimite-tras-quedarse-fuera-de-las-listas-del-psoe-del-29-n.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El delegado del Gobierno en Madrid dimite tras quedarse fuera de las listas del PSOE para el 29-N

sources.body:
El delegado del Gobierno en la Comunidad de Madrid , Francisco Martín, ha presentado su dimisión porque "no se dan las condiciones para seguir ejerciendo su responsabilidad", según han confirmado a RTVE fuentes de la Delegación. Ocupaba el cargo desde marzo de 2023.

Su renuncia se ha producido después de que se quedara fuera de las listas del PSOE al Congreso y el Senado para las elecciones generales del 29-N, a diferencia de otras delegadas del Gobierno que sí irán en esas listas como, por ejemplo, Pilar Bernabé (Valencia) o Adriana Lastra (Asturias).

También se da la circunstancia de que apoyó de forma tácita la candidatura de Enma López en las primarias del pasado julio en las que la exministra de Industria, Comercio y Turismo Reyes Maroto y actual concejal del Ayuntamiento de Madrid fue elegida candidata a la Alcaldía de la capital.

La propia Enma López ha agradecido en X a Martín su labor en estos años "de buen trabajo, compromiso y entrega". "Madrid pierde a un gran servidor público", ha expresado en la red social la edil socialista, que fue apartada de la dirección del grupo municipal en el Ayuntamiento tras su derrota en las primarias.

Se espera que este martes el Consejo de Ministros nombre para el cargo a la actual subdelegada, Pilar Trinidad Núñez .

En las últimas semanas había mantenido un pulso con el Gobierno de la Comunidad de Madrid por su decisión de no desalojar la acampada de la Puerta del Sol como pedía el Ejecutivo de Isabel Díaz Ayuso, que acusó a Martín de actuar de manera ilegal al no ordenar el desalojo de esa acampada.

Además, a principios de esta semana la Delegación del Gobierno en Madrid ordenó una investigación para esclarecer las cargas policiales que se produjeron contra un grupo de profesores que se concentraron a las puertas de un acto de la presidenta madrileña.

Martín también fue objeto de las quejas de los sindicatos policiales por sus críticas a las cargas en las manifestaciones por la educación en la Ciudad Universitaria.

De hecho, Jupol , el sindicato mayoritario de la Policía Nacional, ha celebrado la dimisión de quien ha dejado a los agentes "a los pies de los caballos" tras sus "ataques" a las actuaciones policiales y ha pedido al próximo delegado del Gobierno en Madrid que tenga " menos cálculo político y más seguridad ciudadana ", así como "valentía, responsabilidad y respaldo institucional sin complejos".

Desde que asumió el cargo, Martín ha adquirido un perfil marcado por los enfrentamientos políticos e institucionales con la presidenta de la Comunidad y el alcalde del Ayuntamiento de Madrid, José Luis Martínez Almeida.

"Ayuso debería pedir disculpas y dejar de abochornar a todos los madrileños", dijo Martín tras la polémica por el viaje a México del pasado mes de mayo de la presidenta de la Comunidad .

Militante socialista desde el año 2000 , pasó de responsabilidades técnicas y de gestión en el ámbito público y empresarial a puestos de relevancia en el PSOE y en la Presidencia del Gobierno.

Hasta su llegada a la Delegación, había ejercido como secretario general de la Presidencia , y antes de eso fue director del Departamento de Planificación y Seguimiento de la Actividad Gubernamental de la Presidencia del Gobierno (2020-2021) y director del Gabinete Técnico de la Secretaría General de la Presidencia del Gobierno (2018-2020), compaginando este cargo con el de consejero de Paradores.

stories.headline: Former Catalan minister Toni Comín returns to Catalunya after nine years abroad

sources.body:
El exconseller de Cultura Toni Comín ha cruzado este domingo la frontera de Francia para llegar a Cataluña, nueve años después del referéndum unilateral del 1-O: "Esta batalla la hemos ganado". "El conseller Puig, yo y el presidente Puigdemont volvemos libres a casa", ha dicho en un discurso en la frontera delante del Memorial de la Retirada en Cerbère, en Francia, donde ha iniciado una ruta acompañado de un centenar de familiares, amigos y compañeros de partido, hacia Portbou (Girona), en el Coll de Belitres.

Según ha dicho, "lo último que el Estado español quería era que tres miembros del Govern del 1-O volvieran libres a casa, sin pasar un segundo por la cárcel", gracias a la ley de amnistía.

Por ello, su regreso no es "la victoria definitiva", pero sí un "éxito colectivo" de todo el movimiento. Tras agradecer a su familia y amigos el apoyo durante los años en los que ha residido en Lovaina (Bélgica), Comín ha asegurado que, nueve años después, "la independencia continúa siendo igual de necesaria", por lo que "la lucha continúa y debe continuar".

"Por alto que sea el precio, sigue siendo un objetivo posible, siempre que estemos dispuestos a pagar el precio, democráticamente y pacíficamente, no hace falta decirlo", ha dicho.

El eurodiputado de Junts ha asegurado que el "exilio" les ha hecho más fuertes y ha servido para defender la lucha "por la libertad" y lograr victorias del independentismo en instancias judiciales europeas. En este punto, también ha dado las gracias a su abogado, Gonzalo Boye: "Honor y gloria, sin él hoy no estaría yo aquí".

El recorrido ha empezado en el faro de Cerbère (Francia), donde un centenar de personas han recibido a Comín, acompañado de su hija, con banderas 'esteladas' y con una urna del 1-O. Entre ellas estaban el vicepresidente y portavoz de Junts, Josep Rius, diputados en el Parlament y en el Congreso y la exconsellera del Govern de Puigdemont Meritxell Borràs, entre otros.

El secretario general de Junts, Jordi Turull, no ha acudido con motivo del fallecimiento de su madre, que él mismo ha hecho público a través de Twitter. También estaban el presidente de Òmnium Cultural, Xavier Antich, miembros de la ANC y el eurodiputado de Comuns Jaume Asens, amigo de Comín. A lo largo de la ruta se han sumado más personas, como la expresidenta del Parlament Laura Borràs u Oleguer Pujol y Jordi Pujol, hijos del expresidente Jordi Pujol.

Comín, que regresó este jueves a Madrid para recoger su acta como eurodiputado de Junts, ha reconocido las dificultades de "volver dos veces, que abordó con el expresident Carles Puigdemont, a quien ha definido como su "hermano de exilio".

Según ha explicado, el expresident le dijo, en referencia al día de la investidura del presidente Salvador Illa: "Seguramente seamos las dos únicas personas de la historia que hemos vuelto dos veces del mismo exilio".

Con el regreso de Comín y del exconseller Lluís Puig esta semana, después de que el Supremo levantara las órdenes de detención contra ellos, solamente queda pendiente el de Carles Puigdemont, que se perfila para después de las elecciones generales del 29N.

Toni Comín ha tornat de l'exili aquest diumenge, després de nou anys. Ho ha fet a peu a través de la frontera administrativa que separa Cervera de la Marenda, al Rosselló, i Portbou, a l'Alt Empordà.

L'exconseller ha començat el trajecte cap a les 12 del migdia envoltat de polítics de Junts, familiars, amics i companys de causa que han decidit acompanyar-lo en el retorn a casa després de nou anys d'exili a Bèlgica, els darrers vivint a Lovaina.

"Sembla que no pugui ser" , comentava entre abraçades mentre recorria el camí costerut de poc més d'una hora que uneix el far de Cervera i el coll dels Belitres, on s'ha adreçat als presents.

Al costat d'una urna de l'1 d'Octubre i just sobre la línia de la frontera , Comín ha explicat que "mai havia esperat tants anys una cosa".

Comín torna de l'exili a peu pel coll dels Belitres: "Mai havia esperat tants anys una cosa: avui és una festa, la del retorn" https://t.co/EGdtGATjuk https://t.co/DZQugEisyl

En un discurs que ha durat gairebé mitja hora, ha explicat que la d'avui " és una festa, la del retorn " i ha donat les gràcies als presents i també als que no hi han pogut ser.

Comín ha tingut un record per a Jordi Turull, secretari general de Junts, que no ha pogut assistir a l'acte per la mort de la mare.

En la part més política de les seves paraules, ha reivindicat el camí de l'exili : "Hem guanyat. L'últim que volia l'estat espanyol és que tres membres del govern a l'exili poguessin tornar."

Tornem lliures a casa i no és una victòria personal, és una victòria de tot el moviment independentista.

Assegura que no és la victòria definitiva, però sí que, sense l'exili, no hi hauria hagut l'amnistia. També ha defensat la independència com una causa justa i un objectiu possible "per alt que sigui el preu" .

"L'aprenentatge no ens dissuadeix, fa que ens preparem millor per arribar fins al final", ha afegit.

En aquest punt, ha recordat la figura de Gonzalo Boye , advocat dels exiliats, a qui ha dedicat un "honor i glòria". Assegura que l'estratègia de l'exili li ha "partit l'espinada a l'Estat."

Comín torna de l'exili a peu pel coll dels Belitres: "Mai havia esperat tants anys una cosa: avui és una festa, la del retorn" https://t.co/EGdtGATjuk https://t.co/DZQugEisyl

En un discurs que ha reconegut "més personal que polític", Comín també ha tingut paraules per a Puigdemont, a qui ha definit com un "germà d'exili", i ha fet broma assegurant que són les dues úniques persones que han tornat dos cops de l'exili , en referència al seu pas per Madrid i al retorn fugaç de l'expresident l'agost del 2025.

De fet, Comín ha enviat un missatge a la Junta Electoral, que el va citar a Madrid el dia 22 per jurar la Constitució per poder ser eurodiputat , abans que tornés de l'exili: "Han fracassat".

En la part més personal, ha tingut un record per als seus tres germans , a qui ha agraït que no hagi perdut el contacte amb la família:

L'exili implicava el risc que la família Comín esdevingués més petita i no ha estat així.

També ha explicat que els pròxims dies voldrà visitar el cementiri de Castellterçol, on hi ha enterrats el seu germà i la seva mare, que han mort durant el seu exili.

stories.headline: Barcelona's housing stock is growing by roughly 2,400 homes a year

sources.body:
Panorámica de viviendas en construcción en la ciudad de Barcelona. Foto archivo / MANU MITRU

Barcelona sumó un total de 22.058 viviendas a su parque residencial entre 2019 y 2026 . Un incremento que, desde 2021, se ha mantenido estable en torno a una media de 2.400 viviendas anuales . Es la conclusión a la que llega un estudio del Observatori Metropolità de l’Habitage de Barcelona (O-HB), que concluye que el parque habitacional de Barcelona acanza las 798.663 viviendas en 2026 , mientras que en 2019 la cifra se ubicaba en las 776.605.

Se trata de una estimación a la que ha llegado el Observatori a partir de una metodología propia basada en datos catastrales depurados y estimaciones a escala de parcela. Esto no implica necesariamente que sean nuevas viviendas construidas, dado que el parque puede crecer vía otras fórmulas como la división de pisos, remontas de edificios o con la reconversión de antiguos locales comerciales y oficinas, por ejemplo. Un nivel de detalle en el que no se adentra el informe del O-HB.

El estudio del Observatori explica que las estimaciones varían incluso entre fuentes oficiales. Así, los últimos datos disponibles presentan diferencias superiores a las 100.000 viviendas , dependiendo de la fuente. La estimación más baja contabiliza 701.774 viviendas en la ciudad de Barcelona (Urban Audit, INE, 2024), mientras que la más alta alcanza las 808.751 viviendas (INE, Censo de 2021).

“Las fuentes que se basan en una lectura directa del Catastro (como Urban Audit o Inspire) tienden a infraestimar el parque de viviendas y sitúan las cifras por debajo de la estimación del O-HB”, resume el documento. También se sitúan por debajo los resultados de la Encuesta Sociodemográfica de Barcelona , que, aunque no tiene como finalidad específica el recuento de viviendas, es la única encuesta que ofrece una estimación de estas.

De este modo, los censos son las fuentes que presentan las cifras más elevadas, pero la ruptura metodológica entre 2011 y 2021 dificulta su comparación y la interpretación de su evolución temporal. “La estimación del Censo de 2021, basada en el Catastro, pero con una depuración posterior, es la que más se aproxima a la estimación del O-HB, que sigue una metodología similar (808.751 frente a 798.663 viviendas)”, concluye el estudio.

La actual crisis de la vivienda insta a las administraciones, más allá de regular los precios de los alquileres, de los pisos turísticos o por habitaciones, lograr aumentar la oferta habitacional ante una demanda desbordada. De hecho, los últimos datos del Observatori Metropolità de l’Habitatge señalan que algo más de 1.300.000 catalanes buscan vivienda de forma activa , una cifra que crece año a año . El problema de acceso, claro, hace años que sobrepasó las fronteras de la capital catalana y la previsión es que aún se alargue durante años. Distintos representantes municipales de varias grandes ciudades españolas insistían en un acto sobre el futuro de las áreas metropolitanas este 21 de octubre precisamente en que, incluso con planificación, las promociones de vivienda tardan entre cuatro y cinco años en desarrollarse, por lo que la oferta tardará años en compensar la demanda .
sources.headline: Barcelona incrementa su parque residencial a una velocidad de unas 2.400 viviendas al año

stories.headline: Barcelona lottery outlets warn that centralizing online sales could threaten a major share of their income

sources.body: Neguit entre les administracions de Loteries de l’Estat. La venda de jocs i apostes que fan a través de les seves pàgines web i d’altres plataformes en línia autoritzades, diuen, es troben en perill. I és que, segons expliquen els administradors, la Societat Estatal de Loteries i Apostes de l’Estat (SELAE), que regula els jocs estatals, vol comercialitzar, de manera exclusiva, aquestes vendes a través d’internet. Això, asseguren els administradors, compromet la viabilitat de molts establiments. Loteries i Apostes de l’Estat, però, nega el conflicte i diu que, lluny de voler centralitzar les vendes, s’està analitzant la millor manera perquè les administracions participin en la venda en línia dels productes complint amb els requisits legals, de gestió i d’interès general. També et pot interessar Com compartir un dècim de la Loteria de Nadal per evitar ensurts si toca? Jessica Moreno Cusac 3 minuts de lectura Què passaria amb les comissions de la venda per internet? A Barcelona hi ha més de 250 administracions de loteries. Per cada aposta venuda cobren una comissió que marca l’Estat. Per exemple, per la Loteria Nacional ingressen un 6 %; de la Primitiva, un 5,9 % i del sorteig extraordinari de Nadal, un 4,5 %. Quan la venda és física o a través del web propi del negoci els és molt fàcil saber quants números han venut i, per tant, el que cobraran. També si la venda es fa des de plataformes com Loteros.com. Ara bé, diuen que la cosa es complica si el número es compra directament des del web de Loteries i Apostes de l’Estat. Mònica Elguer, propietària de l’ administració La Suertuda , explica que en aquests casos el comprador pot seleccionar a quina administració destina les comissions i si no ho fa, Loteries i Apostes de l’Estat “teòricament les distribueix entre les administracions adherides”. “El que passa és que sí que és veritat que hi ha hagut algun premi que casualment no estava associat a cap administració”, alerta la Mònica, que qüestiona el model. Perdrien entre el 30 i el 40 % dels ingressos Els administradors temen que l’Estat deixi només la pàgina web de la SELAE per vendre a través d’internet. De fet, algunes s’han associat i han creat la plataforma Defensa Digital (DEDIT) per denunciar l’amenaça de Loteries i Apostes de l’Estat d’imposar un monopoli de la comercialització en línia de la loteria . Calculen que suposaria treure a les administracions el 30 % dels ingressos i abocar-ne milers al tancament, especialment les petites i rurals. A Barcelona, per exemple, Víctor Fernández, director de la Loteria Las Arenas , calcula que la facturació en línia representa entre un 30 i un 40 % del total. Fa uns 11 anys que va començar a oferir la venda en línia amb serveis que van més enllà dels que té la SELAE. “Si compres un dècim a través de la seva pàgina web no el pots compartir, per la nostra web, sí”, explica en Víctor. A més, insisteix que han invertit molts diners a millorar el web i el sistema de vendes. Mònica Elguer planteja una alternativa als plans de la SELAE. Demana que les administracions puguin seguir tenint web pròpia de venda en línia, però amb una regularització i normativa expresses que hi posin ordre i estableixin uns criteris clars. Sobretot, afegeix, pensant en el futur: “A les generacions joves que entren al sector és impensable que els diguis que tenen un negoci que no poden treure a l’exterior a través d’internet”. També et pot interessar 9 coses que has de saber si compres Loteria de Nadal i no vols ensurts a última hora Olga Borràs Boada 4 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: Les administracions de loteries temen perdre la venda en línia, que suposa el 30 % dels ingressos
